data_description: THE anchor source for this lane. Pooled Ionis integrated safety database: 59 trials, 16 distinct 2'-MOE PS ASOs, 3,476 subjects. Verified full text via efetch (132 KB XML) AND the 10-page supplementary PDF via the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles zip endpoint (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC5467133/supplementaryFiles) - all tables text-extractable. Table 1: 16 ASOs with ISIS number, target gene, full 5'->3' sequence, gapmer design (5-10-5 etc.), trial and subject counts - populates oligos.csv directly. Table 2: dose ranges (mg/week) and treatment duration by indication. Table 3: incidence of confirmed platelet reductions, phase 1-3, panel A (normal-baseline subjects) and panel B, cross-tabulated by 5 platelet-count bands (LLN-100, <100-75, <75-50, <50-25, <25 K/uL) and 2 relative bands (<0.7xBSLN, <0.5xBSLN) against placebo, ASO total, and SIX dose bands (>0-75, >75-175, >175-275, >275-375, >375-475, >475 mg/week) - this table alone is the dose-response backbone. Table 4: mipomersen-specific confirmed post-baseline platelet reductions, total/6-month/1-year phase 3 RCTs vs placebo. Table 5: proportion of ASOs with >10% incidence of >30% platelet decline, by dose band. Table 6: platelet reductions stratified by antithrombotic co-medication use. Table 7: bleeding-event incidence, mipomersen vs placebo. Fig 1: platelet level over time (percent change and absolute count) for ISIS 104838 in a 12-week phase 2 RA trial. Supplementary Tables S4 (DDI trials), S6 (42 randomized placebo-controlled trials, full dose x threshold grid), S7 (on- vs post-treatment), S8 (subject-level meta-analysis of mean % change by dose), S9 (subject-level meta-analysis of incidence), S11 (bleeding events), S12 (coagulation-time abnormalities).
title: The Effects of 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Containing Antisense Oligonucleotides on Platelets in Human Clinical Trials

data_description: Verified: HTTP 200, 121 pages, 49 pages containing platelet content, parsed with PyMuPDF. The definitive public-domain record of volanesorsen's dose-limiting thrombocytopenia, and it supersedes the paywalled APPROACH (NEJM) and COMPASS (Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol) primary papers. Table 37 (p91): 'Summary of Confirmed Nadir Post-Baseline Platelet Counts in Study CS6 (APPROACH)' - full 5-band nadir distribution (100-140k, 75-100k, 50-75k, 25-50k, 0-25k per mm3) for placebo n=33 vs volanesorsen n=33, plus <140,000 and <100,000 cumulative rows (24/33 = 75.0% vs 8/33 = 24.2%; <100,000 in 15/32 = 46.9% vs 0%). Table 38 (p92): same for Study CS16 (COMPASS), N=113 - NOTE this one is an embedded image, needs vision extraction. Table 39 (p94): fully text-extractable - dose, average baseline platelet count, average nadir platelet count and average nadir % change from baseline, split by body weight <70 kg (N=11, nadir 76 x10^9/L, -62.3%) vs >=70 kg (N=8, nadir 126 x10^9/L, -43.3%). Table 40 (p98): per-patient listing of every platelet decrease to <50,000/mm3 across CS2, CS6 and CS16 with preferred term, platelet nadir, time to onset, duration, associated bleeding events and discontinuation action. Table 41 (p99): per-patient nadir count, initial monitoring frequency, dose regimen at onset, time to decline from >100,000 to nadir (days), time to recover to >50,000 and to >140,000 - text-extractable, spans CS2/CS6/CS16/CS7. Table 22 (p60): actions taken in patients with low platelet count in CS6. Figure 20: platelet decline time course reaching a plateau ~30% below baseline. Narrative (p90-92) adds CS6 mean nadir 134,000/mm3 at Week 25 vs 207,000 placebo, mean change -48,000 vs +25,000, AE incidences (platelet count decreased 30% vs 3%; thrombocytopenia 12% vs 0% in CS6; 4% vs 5% and 13% vs 5% in CS16), 2 grade-4 (<25,000/mm3) events leading to discontinuation, and CS7 open-label figures (platelet count decreased 18%, thrombocytopenia 9%).
title: Waylivra (volanesorsen) EPAR Public Assessment Report

data_description: VERIFIED: full-text JATS XML, 142,752 bytes (also PMC page HTTP 200). Highest-volume in-vitro human platelet source in the lane. Table 2 'Design of the tool ONs' gives 12 oligonucleotides with COMPLETE 5'->3' sequences and explicit PS linkage marks (ODN2395_Thio, ODN2395 non-PS, (AC)5 through (AC)11, and (AC)8/9/10 LNA) — directly populates oligos.csv incl. ps_count and length_nt. Per-compound human platelet readouts: Fig 1A PAC-1 and Fig 1B P-selectin on human platelets, all 12 ONs at 10 uM (10 min, vs 20 uM ADP / 20 uM TRAP controls, n=5); Fig 1C (AC)8 concentration-response with the text stating 1 uM as the lowest active concentration; Fig 2A-C GPVI surface-plasmon-resonance binding for all ONs at 10 uM vs bovine collagen I control, Fig 2D (AC)8 concentration-response with half-maximal GPVI binding ~2 uM; Fig 3B-C PF4/KKO-antibody ELISA per ON expressed as % maximal heparin binding (n=4), bell-shaped curve for (AC)11. Adjacent non-platelet rows (is_platelet_specific=FALSE): Fig 4 human primary bone-marrow ATP content, Fig 6 human whole-blood IL-8 (>20-fold for ODN2395 Thio; 8-13 fold for (AC)n at 50 uM) and MCP-1 (3-4 fold). Table 1 documents the five-assay battery. LICENCE: CC-BY 4.0 confirmed from the article licence field (ali:license_ref, creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) => schema class `cc_by`, raw per-compound values reproducible with attribution.
title: Assessing single-stranded oligonucleotide drug-induced effects in vitro reveals key risk factors for thrombocytopenia (Sewing et al.)

data_description: Verified: HTTP 200, 10.2 MB, 223 pages, 64 pages with platelet content (IMPORTANT: accessdata.fda.gov returns 404 to a default curl UA - a browser User-Agent is required). Contains Evelyn Mentari's full Clinical Safety Review section 8.5 'Thrombocytopenia' with the most granular public inotersen platelet data anywhere. Table 24 (p140): subjects with decreased platelet measurements, central and local lab values, Studies CS2 and CS3 (image - vision extraction). Table 25 (p141): the explicit bimodal typology - 'Rare' (rapid onset, severe, catastrophic fatal bleeding) vs 'Common' (gradual slow decline, often mild) - text-extractable and maps directly onto the schema's grade-3 vs grade-1 split. Table 31 (p154): antiplatelet antibody test results cross-tabulated against platelet-count change, Study CS2. Table 32 (p155): subjects with nadir platelet count <75 x10^9/L AND treatment-emergent positive antiplatelet antibodies. Table 33 (p159): post-baseline nadir platelets and dose exposure by baseline platelet count. Table 34 (p160): FULLY TEXT-EXTRACTABLE - frequency and relative risk of nadir <75 x10^9/L by baseline platelet count: CS2 10/39 (25.6%) for baseline <200 x10^9/L vs 3/73 (4.1%) for >=200, RR 6.2; longitudinal CS2+CS3 15/39 (38.5%) vs 4/73 (5.5%), RR 7.0. Table 35 (p162): subjects who paused dosing due to platelet count <75 x10^9/L. Narrative p141 gives CS2 <100 x10^9/L in 28/112 (25.0%) inotersen vs 1/60 (1.7%) placebo; <75 x10^9/L in 16/112 (14.3%) vs 0/60; <25 x10^9/L (severe) in 3 (2.7%); 71% of subjects had a >=30% post-treatment platelet decline. Individual clinical summaries follow for all 3 severe-thrombocytopenia subjects including the fatal intracranial haemorrhage. The companion OtherR.pdf (232 pp, 5.6 MB, same URL pattern) is a Division of Hematology Products consult with its own Tables 2-7 and 14-17 restating the sponsor's Summary of Clinical Safety tables 64/67/69 - overlapping but independently citable (e.g. its narrative gives <100 x10^9/L as 26/112 = 23.2% vs 1/60 = 1.6%, and a 22.4% incidence-rate difference, 95% CI 13.9-31.0).
title: FDA Clinical Safety Review, Tegsedi (inotersen) NDA 211172 (Medical Review; companion DHP haematology consult in OtherR)

data_description: VERIFIED: full-text XML 96,724 bytes; publisher PDF also downloaded (3.1 MB, 13 pp) from haematologica.org/article/download/haematol.2020.260059/72951. Five PS ASOs, three 2'MOE (487660 = no clinical platelet effect, 104838 = phenotype-1 associated, 501861 = unknown) and two CpG (120704, ODN 2395); Ionis Pharmaceuticals is a co-author, so these are Ionis compound numbers. NUMERIC VALUES IN PROSE (not just figures): Fig 3A human PRP P-selectin at 5 uM, 9 donors — vehicle 10+/-2%, 104838 19+/-3%, 501861 20+/-3%, 120704 38+/-3%, ODN 2395 38+/-4%, 487660 no increase; Fig 3B whole blood (8 donors) +/- SYK inhibitor PRT-060318; Fig 3C-D per-donor GPVI MFI correlated with P-selectin (7 donors); Fig 3E-F SDF1-alpha release in PRP and WB at 1, 5 and 10 uM (4 donors); Fig 7F fluorescence-polarisation GPVI binding, KD ~0.2-1.5 uM for all five ASO, with human serum albumin KD stated per compound in text (487660 12.9 uM, 104838 24 uM, 501861 26 uM); Fig 2 immuno-EM ASO uptake in human washed platelets at 5 uM; Fig 6-7 SYK-dependent platelet-neutrophil and platelet-monocyte aggregates; Suppl Fig S1 LDH non-cytotoxicity at 1 and 5 uM; Fig 1A human cord-blood-derived megakaryocyte proplatelet counts (120704 117+/-5 vs vehicle 79+/-7). CAVEATS: Table 1 (the ASO sequences/chemistry) is a bitmap <graphic> in both XML and PDF — sequences are NOT text-extractable and must remain TBD; and the PDF text layer renders every 'uM' as 'mM' via symbol-font substitution (the XML has the correct uM) — use the XML units. LICENCE: CC-BY-NC 4.0 confirmed from the article licence field; the NC clause conflicts with a CC-BY dataset release, so treat as fair-use summary statistics.
title: Sequence-specific 2'-O-methoxyethyl antisense oligonucleotides activate human platelets through glycoprotein VI, triggering formation of platelet-leukocyte aggregates (Lundberg Slingsby et al.)

data_description: 442 pp, 460 platelet/thrombocytopenia hits. Applicant Table 95 (p.306) Grade 3/4 decreased platelets and bleeding within 7 days, Study MDS3001 Phase 2 + Phase 3: Grade 3/4 platelets 77/118 (65.3%) imetelstat Ph3 vs 5/59 (8.5%) placebo, 33/57 (57.9%) Ph2, 110/175 (62.9%) pooled; with any bleeding 9 (7.6%) / 0 / 8 (14.0%) / 17 (9.7%); Grade 3/4 bleeding 0 / 0 / 2 (3.5%) / 2 (1.1%). Table 99 (p.310) thrombocytopenia and hemorrhagic events BY DOSE LEVEL across the whole development program — low dose N=54: 11 (21%); standard N=190: 137 (73%); high N=296: 184 (62%); placebo N=59: 6 (10%); hemorrhage 12 (22%) / 50 (26%) / 153 (52%) / 7 (12%); Grade 3-4 hemorrhage 1 (1.9%) / 11 (6%) / 62 (21%) / 1 (1.7%); fatal hemorrhage 0 / 0 / 5 (1.7%) / 0. Figure 36 (p.288) mean platelet count by study arm at baseline and over treatment. Resolution kinetics p.278: 183/212 (86.3%) Grade 3/4 events resolved to Grade <=2 and 40/47 (85.1%) Grade 4 events to Grade <=3 within 4 weeks, vs 4/9 (44.4%) placebo; Ph2 median time to onset of Grade 3/4 decreased platelets 4.0 weeks (range 2.0-89.7). Placebo-arm data p.304 (any-grade 10.2%, Grade 3/4 8.5%, Grade 4 3.4%). Mechanism is telomerase-inhibitor myelosuppression, NOT phosphorothioate platelet binding — flag in notes.
title: FDA Multi-Discipline Review and Evaluation, NDA 217779 Rytelo (imetelstat)

data_description: Verified: HTTP 200, 142 pages, 42 pages with platelet content, PyMuPDF text-extractable. The EU regulator's independent read of NEURO-TTR (CS2) and its open-label extension (CS3), with numbers that do not all appear in the FDA review or the NEJM paper. p90: TEAE incidences by preferred term - thrombocytopenia 13.4% inotersen vs 1.7% placebo; platelet count decreased 10.7% vs 0%; anaemia 13.4% vs 3.3%. p93 (Assessment p92): mean platelet count decline from baseline of 20% at 3 months, 24% at 6 months and 26% at Week 65 (EOT) in CS2; documents an initial RISE in platelets at Week 2/3 attributed to hsCRP-driven reactive thrombocytosis - a distinct effect_direction=increase row. p93-95: severe-thrombocytopenia case detail with nadir <10 x10^9/L concomitant with fatal intracranial haemorrhage; monitoring changed from every 2-3 weeks to weekly as a consequence. p94: immune-mediation evidence - all subjects with grade 4 thrombocytopenia were positive for treatment-emergent antiplatelet IgG; 4 of 8 grade 3/4 subjects also positive for anti-platelet-surface-glycoprotein (GP IIb/IIIa) antibodies; anti-PF4 IgA in one and anti-PF4 IgM in two; CS3 anti-PF4 IgM 20% placebo-inotersen vs 0% inotersen-inotersen. p95: re-initiation in 16 recovered subjects with prior platelet decreases <75 x10^9/L led to recurrent thrombocytopenia in all but one. p88: 4 discontinuations for thrombocytopenia as an AE of special interest. p101: bleeding-event rate 33% vs 24% by anticoagulant co-medication.
title: Tegsedi (inotersen) EPAR Public Assessment Report

data_description: VERIFIED: full-text XML 87,249 bytes. The foundational GPVI-mechanism paper. Human in-vitro panels (mouse panels 1d-1e and 3a-3d belong to the animal lane and must be excluded here): Fig 1a ODN2395 binding to human platelets at 50 nM vs 1-10 uM non-PS ODN2395 (n=6); Fig 1b CD62P/P-selectin on human WASHED platelets, concentration-resolved 50 nM to 10 uM (n=5); Fig 1c platelet AGGREGATION in human PRP at 5 uM ODN2395 vs 5 uM ADP / 1 ug/mL collagen (n=6); Fig 1f ODN2395-coated-bead binding/activation of washed platelets; Fig 1g platelet-monocyte aggregate formation in human whole blood at 1 and 5 uM (n=10); Fig 1h adhesion/spreading on 30 ug/mL fibrinogen; Fig 1i intraplatelet ROS at 5 uM vs 10 ug/mL CRP-XL; Fig 2a thrombus formation under 400/s flow on collagen/fibrinogen at 5 uM; Fig 2d Syk (Bay 61-3606) and Src (PP2) inhibitor blockade; Fig 2f-2g GPVI-Fc bead binding and GPVI pull-down; Fig 2h platelets from two GPVI-DEFICIENT PATIENTS show no binding or activation up to 10 uM (a mechanistically decisive negative row); Fig 2j GPVI dimer formation at 5 uM by 204-FAB. Additional compounds: Fig 3e PS-modified miR-322 concentration-dependent PAC-1 binding (n=3); Fig 3f-3g G3139/oblimersen-induced activation and binding in whole blood at 1 uM input vs 10 uM non-PS G3139 (n=6), with washed-platelet activity stated at 50-100 nM. CLINICAL-RELEVANCE ANCHOR for fold_Cmax: the paper states the measured human G3139 plasma concentration after i.v. infusion was 0.84 +/- 0.6 uM (Marcucci et al.), and that PS-ASO plasma concentrations approach 5 uM. Sequences for ODN2395 (PS and non-PS), the scrambled PS ODN, and PS ODN TTAGGG are given verbatim in Methods. LICENCE: CC-BY-NC-SA 3.0 from the article licence field (Europe PMC license = 'cc by-nc-sa') — the NC and SA clauses conflict with a CC-BY dataset release, so treat as fair-use summary statistics.
title: Phosphorothioate backbone modifications of nucleotide-based drugs are potent platelet activators (Flierl et al.)

data_description: VERIFIED: 190,149 chars of PMC full-text XML, both tables parsed as machine-readable rows. Valenzuela, Ayuso, Buyssens et al. Table 1 = 7 tool ASOs with FULL 5'->3' SEQUENCES written residue-by-residue with explicit phosphorothioate linkage markers and case-encoded chemistry (ODN2395, ODN2395-PO, ISIS104838, ISIS104838-PS, RTR5001, RTR5001-PS, RTR5001-PO), plus modification class (PS / unmodified / 2'MOE-PS-2'MOE / LNA-PS-LNA), length (14-22 nt), PS load (0-21) and platelet effect — an unusually clean PS-count-vs-effect predictor set for oligos.csv. Table 2 = cross-species matrix of in-vivo and in-vitro platelet response for all 7 ASOs across Gottingen minipig, NHP and human (in-vivo effect, activation assay, aggregometry), e.g. ISIS104838 'thrombocytopenia' in human and NHP vs RTR5001 'no effect' in human, NHP and minipig. title: Platelet Activation by Antisense Oligonucleotides (ASOs) in the Gottingen Minipig, including an Evaluation of Glycoprotein VI (GPVI) and Platelet Factor 4 (PF4) Ontogeny

data_description: VERIFIED: the PMC/efetch record is ABSTRACT-ONLY (10 kB, no <body>) and the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returns nothing, but the Europe PMC PDF-render URL above returns HTTP 200 with a real 1,218,316-byte 10-page PDF that parses to 51,319 characters of full text via PyMuPDF — this is the route that works, do not use efetch for this one. The best APTAMER-modality source in the lane, and the only one covering the PF4/HIT-like idiosyncratic axis with human platelets. Four aptamers of different length and secondary structure (15mer-DNA thrombin aptamer, 44mer-DNA activated-protein-C aptamer, 57mer-RNA tetracycline aptamer, 77mer-RNA FMN aptamer) plus a construct series (10mer-ssDNA, 21mer-hairpin RNA, 21mer-dsDNA and two other 21mer DNA secondary structures, 45mer double-stem-loop RNA I and II, the sequence-matched 45mer double-stem-loop DNA, 45mer-polyA, 45mer-polyC, single nucleotides, cellular RNA +/- RNase A). PER-COMPOUND NUMERIC VALUES IN PROSE with the concentration at which they occur, on human gel-filtered platelets (50 x 10^9/L, flow cytometry): heparin 4.44-fold +/-0.15; cellular RNA 3.69-fold +/-1.09 at 0.63 ug/mL, falling to 1.25-fold +/-0.29 after RNase A (P=.0037); 57mer-RNA tetracycline aptamer 2.48-fold +/-0.63 and 77mer-RNA FMN aptamer 2.07-fold +/-0.52, both maximal at 0.63 ug/mL; 44mer-DNA protein C aptamer 2.59-fold +/-0.35 at 5 ug/mL; 15mer-DNA thrombin aptamer only 3.57-fold +/-1.1 and only at 320 ug/mL; polyA, polyC and single nucleotides no enhancement. Fig 5D EIA optical densities of human anti-PF4/heparin IgG against PF4/aptamer complexes (PF4/heparin control OD 1.130+/-0.143; 44mer aptamer 1.098+/-0.140 over 5-30 ug/mL; 15mer aptamer only 0.431+/-0.064 at 40 ug/mL; reduced to 0.593+/-0.203 by 660 ug/mL heparin, P<.0001) plus a functional heparin-induced-platelet-activation assay with human HIT sera. Sequences and mfold secondary structures for every construct are in Fig 1. LICENCE: ASH copyright, free to read; Europe PMC isOpenAccess=N — free-to-read but NOT open-licensed, so reproduce as summary statistics only.
title: Complex formation with nucleic acids and aptamers alters the antigenic properties of platelet factor 4 (Jaax et al.)

data_description: 44 pp, 81 platelet hits. Sec 4.2 Table: full 5-band platelet monitoring/dosing algorithm (>=140 normal; 100-139; 75-99 pause >=4 wk; 50-74 pause + every 2-3 day monitoring; <50 discontinue + glucocorticoids). Sec 4.3 contraindication <140 x10^9/L. Sec 4.4 lower body weight (<70 kg) more prone; discontinue antiplatelet/NSAID/anticoagulant <75, must stop <50. Sec 4.8: pooled APPROACH+CS7 platelet count decreased 25 (29%), thrombocytopenia 18 (21%). APPROACH pivotal: confirmed reductions below 140 x10^9/L in 75% volanesorsen vs 24% placebo; below 100 x10^9/L in 47%; 5 discontinuations for platelet levels including 2 with counts <25 x10^9/L and 3 between 50 and 75 x10^9/L. CS16: platelet count decreased 11 (33%) vs 1 (3%), thrombocytopenia 4 (12%) vs 0. Open-label extension CS7: below 140 x10^9/L in 52/66 (79%) overall and 37/50 (74%) treatment-naive; 11 discontinuations for thrombocytopenia/platelet events; platelet count decreased 16 (24%), thrombocytopenia 14 (21%). Sec 5.3 ANIMAL: severe thrombocytopenia in individual monkeys in the 9-month study at clinically relevant exposures; decline was not acute and fell below 50,000 cells/uL; counts recovered after cessation but fell below 50,000 again on re-treatment in some monkeys.
title: EMA Waylivra (volanesorsen) SmPC / Annex I Product Information

data_description: VERIFIED: PMC page HTTP 200 and NCBI efetch returns 76,475 bytes of full-text XML with a complete <body>. NOTE the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint 404s for this PMCID — use NCBI efetch db=pmc, not Europe PMC. Human washed platelets and PRP from healthy donors. Two non-targeting ASOs with FULL SEQUENCES GIVEN IN METHODS: NC5 PS-ASO 5'-G*C*G*A*C*T*A*T*A*C*G*C*G*C*A*A*T*A*T*G-3' (20mer, full PS) and its 2'-MOE/PS congener NC5 2'OMe/PS with explicit per-residue modification marks — both directly usable for oligos.csv. Comparators: PC-3 prostate-cancer genomic DNA, a four-member single-stranded pre-miRNA mixture, and two protein controls (thrombospondin-1, EGF). Readouts, per compound and concentration: Fig 1 fluorescence and electron microscopy of oligonucleotide uptake by human platelets (labelled 20mer) and dose-dependent potentiation of low-dose-thrombin platelet aggregation by PS- and MOE/PS-ASO and gDNA (washed platelets at 3 x 10^8/mL); Fig 2 flow-cytometric P-selectin-positive platelets after PS-ASO, MOE/PS-ASO, gDNA, pre-miRNA, TSP-1 or EGF, with abrogation by a TLR-7/-8/-9 antagonist (mechanistically distinct from the GPVI axis of the other sources — worth capturing in notes); Fig 3A EX-VIVO PLATELET COUNT in healthy-donor platelets before and after PS-ASO exposure at 16 uM and 24 uM, n=10 donors with each donor line-matched. CAVEAT: the prose repeatedly writes 'mM' where the methods and figure axes mean uM (e.g. '24 mM' = 24 uM) — a unit typo carried through the article; do not transcribe literally. LICENCE: the PMC permissions block states only 'available for text mining... may also be used consistent with the principles of fair use' — no CC licence, so summary statistics / derived features only.
title: Antisense oligonucleotides and nucleic acids generate hypersensitive platelets (Zaslavsky et al.)

data_description: Verified full text via efetch (177 KB XML, license cc by-nc). The lane's NEGATIVE-CONTROL source and the direct chemistry contrast to the unconjugated gapmers in Crooke 2017 - GalNAc conjugation cuts the dose ~10-20x and the platelet signal disappears entirely. Table 1: eight unique GalNAc3-conjugated PS 2'-MOE ASOs with ISIS ID, RNA target (APOC3, LPA, CFB, ANGPTL3, HBV S, KLKB1, AGT, GHR), full 5'->3' sequence with the L=GalNAc3 prefix, length, design (5-10-5 MOE, PS vs PO/PS backbone), and placebo/active/total n per phase 1 HV-RCT - populates oligos.csv for 8 more compounds including pelacarsen's parent (LPA 681257), olezarsen's parent (APOC3 678354), and IONIS-FB-LRx (CFB 696844). Table 5: 'Incidence of Abnormal Laboratory Test Results in Weekly Multidose Regimen Cohort (N=157)' - the Hematology block gives Platelets <100 K/mm3 and <75 K/mm3 as 0 (0.0%) for placebo (n=36), total ASO (n=121) and each of five dose bands (>0-10, >10-20, >20-40, >40-60, >60 mg/week) - i.e. 14 clean grade-0 rows at named doses. Figures also give mean platelet counts over time and individual-subject platelet spaghetti plots by dose level (placebo, >0-10, >10-20, >20-40, >40-60, >60 mg). Table 4 supplies the cohort demographics/denominators.
title: Integrated Assessment of the Clinical Performance of GalNAc3-Conjugated 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Antisense Oligonucleotides in Phase I Development

data_description: 271 pp, 52 platelet hits. High scientific value as a SPECIES-TRANSLATION CONTRAST: the human Kynamro label contains zero platelet/thrombocytopenia/bleeding content (verified), yet the 1-year cynomolgus monkey study at 30 mg/kg/week (~10x clinical exposure) produced thrombocytopenia in 3 high-dose monkeys requiring dosing holidays of various durations, with platelet counts recovering on drug withdrawal in 2 of 3. Per-animal detail: HD female #5506 sacrificed moribund on Day 271 (Week 39) while on a platelet-driven dosing holiday (last dose Day 239), with a 30-minute post-venipuncture bleed, widespread multifocal hemorrhage at postmortem; animals #5007 and #5506 had the greatest platelet reductions AND the greatest up-regulation of the platelet activation marker CD62P, alongside decreased plasma C3 (complement consumption) — the review proposes complement-mediated platelet activation, increased consumption and splenic removal, with splenomegaly and platelet sequestration; #5505 and #5506 showed macrophage/histiocyte extravascular destruction of RBCs and/or platelets (HLH-like). Also contains a lifetime mouse study and a named mouse surrogate oligo, ISIS 147764, usable as an additional compound. Same 2'-MOE full-PS gapmer chemistry class as inotersen — a within-chemistry comparator.
title: FDA Pharmacology/Toxicology Review, NDA 203568 Kynamro (mipomersen), R. Wange Ph.D.

data_description: Verified full text via efetch (88 KB XML, license cc by-nc-sa). The Ionis integrated safety assessment named in the lane brief, and the dataset's animal-to-human translation anchor for this endpoint. Table 2: 'Incidence of abnormal laboratory test results in healthy human volunteers' with a hematology block including platelets, stratified by dose group. Table 1: the matching incidence table for nonhuman primates (13-week dosing). CAVEAT - Tables 1 and 2 are embedded JPEG graphics (mt2016136t1.jpg / mt2016136t2.jpg), not XHTML, so they need page-image vision extraction; I verified the images fetch cleanly (HTTP 200, 518 KB for t2) from https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/instance/5112040/bin/mt2016136t2.jpg. Figure 4 IS described in text and gives mean +/- SE platelet counts by dose group over time for (a) nonhuman primates, ULN 677 K/mm3, up to 13 weeks and (b) healthy human volunteers, LLN 140 / ULN 400 K/mm3, up to 6 weeks, with each data point representing >=10 subjects, 4 ASOs and 4 independent studies - directly comparable NHP-vs-human rows on the same axis. Figure 1 documents the subject-count distribution and sequence diversity of the 2'-MOE ASOs in the translational safety set.
title: Integrated Safety Assessment of 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Chimeric Antisense Oligonucleotides in NonHuman Primates and Healthy Human Volunteers

data_description: VERIFIED: full-text XML 116,463 bytes. Two unmodified DNA thrombin-binding aptamers (HD1, 15mer G-quadruplex, exosite I; HD22, 29mer, exosite II) tested on HUMAN WASHED PLATELETS and HUMAN PRP from healthy donors. Per-aptamer, per-agonist, per-concentration aggregation data: Fig 1 thrombin-induced aggregation in WP and PRP across an aptamer concentration range (median with box plots and quartiles, and Fig 1 carries a real <table> of values); Fig 2 collagen-induced (2 ug/mL) aggregation at 3 uM aptamer in WP and PRP (mean +/- SD); Fig 3 ristocetin-induced aggregation at 3 uM (1 mg/mL ristocetin in WP, 0.75 mg/mL in PRP); Fig 6 whole-human-blood thrombus formation in the T-TAS microchip flow chamber (T10 occlusion times); Fig 7 atheroma-chip thrombi at 15 uM. Table 1 gives measured dissociation constants of both aptamer-thrombin complexes. VALUE FOR THIS DATASET: these are full-phosphodiester, unmodified DNA aptamers — the exact negative-control chemistry the rubric needs, since they show NO agonist activity on human platelets (effect_direction on collagen- and ristocetin-induced aggregation is unchanged/decrease, not activation), giving well-sourced grade-0 aptamer rows to balance the PS-ASO grade-2/3 rows. Note the effect is anticoagulant inhibition of thrombin-induced aggregation, so effect_direction is decrease for a mechanistic reason, not a toxicity signal — record that distinction in notes. LICENCE: CC-BY 4.0 confirmed from the article licence field => schema class `cc_by`.
title: Comparison of Effects of Anti-thrombin Aptamers HD1 and HD22 on Aggregation of Human Platelets, Thrombin Generation, Fibrin Formation, and Thrombus Formation (Derszniak et al.)

data_description: Verified full text via efetch (132 KB XML, license CC BY - the cleanest redistribution terms of any journal source in this lane). THE ONLY SOURCE I COULD FIND ANYWHERE WITH QUANTITATIVE EPLONTERSEN PLATELET DATA - the Wainua label and the NEURO-TTRansform JAMA paper (PMC10540057) both contain zero platelet mentions. Because it is a within-patient switch design it yields a paired inotersen-vs-eplontersen contrast on identical subjects, which is far stronger evidence for a chemistry/conjugation effect than any between-trial comparison. Extractable: baseline mean (SD) platelet count 228.x x10^9/L; mean (SD) reduction in platelet count from baseline at Week 35 during the inotersen treatment period (-18.x%); mean nadir reduction on inotersen -40.x% versus -3.x% after switching to eplontersen; recovery of mean platelet count to baseline level over a 22-week period after the switch, stable thereafter; incidence of platelet count below the lower limit of normal (<140 x10^9/L) at any post-baseline timepoint 54.x%; no patient on either drug reached <25 x10^9/L and none discontinued or withdrew for low platelet count. Table 2 'Summary of TEAEs' is flagged as containing platelet/thrombocytopenia rows. Fig 2 plots percentage change in platelet count across the inotersen period and after the switch to eplontersen. Table 3 gives plasma PK for both agents, allowing dose/exposure to be attached to each platelet row.
title: Switching from inotersen to eplontersen in patients with hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis

data_description: VERIFIED: full-text XML 112,216 bytes. Human citrated and heparinised whole blood spiked directly with four oligonucleotides, all with FULL SEQUENCES in machine-readable Table 1 'List of used oligonucleotides': NU172 (26mer anti-thrombin DNA aptamer, a genuine clinical-stage therapeutic aptamer), its complementary antidote AD (26mer), and two non-sense controls NS and NS_AD (26mer each). Concentrations 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 uM aptamer plus 1.0 uM antidote. Platelet-relevant readouts: Fig 8 beta-thromboglobulin (a platelet alpha-granule release marker, i.e. a direct platelet_activation readout) by ELISA at 0 and 30 min in an in-vitro rotation model, alongside TAT complex and fibrinopeptide A; Fig 9 automated PLATELET COUNT (plus erythrocytes and leukocytes) in the same human blood before and after 30 min incubation, reported as no significant difference from baseline — a clean, well-sourced grade-0 platelet_count row for the aptamer modality in human blood, with the honest caveat that the article attributes the observed beta-TG rise to the circulation itself rather than to the oligonucleotide. Figs 2-7 give clotting times by piezo and ball coagulometer per aptamer concentration (readout_category = coagulation, is_platelet_specific = FALSE). Ranked medium rather than high because the row count is modest and much of it is coagulation rather than platelet, but it is one of very few sources supplying human in-vitro NEGATIVE controls for an unmodified-DNA therapeutic aptamer. title: Application of Piezo-Based Measuring System for Evaluation of Nucleic Acid-Based Drugs Influencing the Coagulation (Kunnakattu et al.)

data_description: Label sec 5.1 'Thrombocytopenia and Coagulation Abnormalities': 24 of 146 (16%) SPINRAZA-treated patients with high, normal or unknown baseline platelet count developed a platelet level below the lower limit of normal vs 10 of 72 (14%) sham-controlled; in Study 2, two SPINRAZA-treated patients developed platelet counts less than 50,000 cells/uL, with a lowest recorded level of 10,000 cells/uL on study day 28; decreases also observed in the High Dose Regimen group. Label sec 6.1 adverse-reaction table (SPINRAZA 12 mg N=84 vs sham N=42) includes Epistaxis 7% vs 0%. Medical Review sec 8.4.6.2.1 (p.77) adds non-redundant numbers: in Study CS3B, 6 of 56 (11%) nusinersen subjects had a platelet level below LLN vs 0 of 28 controls; across all nusinersen subjects 3 of 145 (2%) had thrombocytopenia <100 x10^9/L; no subject had a count <50 x10^9/L; no thrombocytopenia-related adverse events; 5 of 173 (3%) had a hemorrhagic complication of lumbar puncture. Same page carries a regulator-sourced DRISAPERSEN comparator: mild thrombocytopenia in controlled studies but severe thrombocytopenia <20 x10^9/L in 2% of subjects after 10-29 months of exposure (n=223 exposed >=1 yr) — a bonus compound with a public-domain platelet value. Only intrathecal-delivery rows in the lane.

data_description: Verified: the NEJM pivotal trial is retrievable as a free NIHMS author manuscript in PMC (efetch returned 89 KB of full-text XML; the PMC article page returns HTTP 200, 342 KB). The primary publication behind the boxed warning, and the source of the fatal event. Table 2 'Summary of Adverse Events', N=112 inotersen vs N=60 placebo, includes serious adverse events related to trial regimen: thrombocytopenia 2 (2%) vs 0, intracranial hemorrhage 1 (<1%) vs 0, with the footnote stating that patient had a fatal intracranial hemorrhage associated with grade 4 thrombocytopenia. Results text supplies further extractable per-measurement values: thrombocytopenia as a serious AE in 3 patients (3%); confirmed post-baseline platelet count below 140,000 per mm3 in 60/112 (54%) inotersen vs 8/60 (13%) placebo (cross-referenced to Table S10 of the Supplementary Appendix); platelet counts below 25,000 per mm3 in 3 patients (3%); a platelet count of less than 10,000 per mm3 in the patient with fatal intracranial haemorrhage; no thrombocytopenia below 50,000 per mm3 after weekly platelet monitoring was instituted; 2 patients dose-reduced to 150 mg weekly for platelet decline; and antiplatelet IgG present in each of the 3 severe cases with recovery on glucocorticoids, with heparin-induced-thrombocytopenia mechanism and effects on platelet production explicitly ruled out. NOTE: no open license on the author manuscript - set redistribution to verify and prefer the FDA/EMA public-domain restatements of the same figures where they exist.

data_description: ABSTRACT VERIFIED AND READ IN FULL via efetch (publisher full text is Cloudflare-403 at liebertpub.com/journals.sagepub.com; Europe PMC lists it 'Subscription required'; no PMC deposit; OpenAlex oa_status=closed — there is no open copy). Narayanan/Curtis et al. This is the single most lane-specific source in the literature: the definitive human anti-platelet-antibody characterization of inotersen ITP. Extractable per-measurement values, all locus 'Abstract': mean platelet counts remained >=140 x10^9/L in 50% and >=100 x10^9/L in 80% of NEURO-TTR inotersen subjects at 300 mg/week; grade 4 thrombocytopenia (<25 x10^9/L) in 3 subjects, one fatal intracranial hemorrhage, two recovered on corticosteroids + discontinuation; investigational subsets n=17 placebo / n=31 inotersen (NEURO-TTR) and n=33 (OLE); direct myelotoxicity, consumptive coagulopathy and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia each RULED OUT (three explicit negative mechanism rows); antiplatelet IgG detected at BASELINE in 5 of 31 (16%) inotersen subjects, 4 of whom later developed grade 1-2 thrombocytopenia; 24 subjects developed TREATMENT-EMERGENT antiplatelet IgG, of whom 2 developed grade 2 and 3 developed grade 4; antiplatelet IgG in 2 of the 3 grade-4 subjects specifically targeted GPIIb/IIIa; plasma IL-23 and APRIL often above normal range at baseline.
title: Underlying Immune Disorder May Predispose Some Transthyretin Amyloidosis Subjects to Inotersen-Mediated Thrombocytopenia

data_description: Sec 6.1 Trial 1 (FCS) adverse-reaction table: Decreased platelet count 5 of 43 (12%) TRYNGOLZA vs 1 of 23 (4%) placebo — listed among the most common adverse reactions. Sec 6.1 Laboratory Tests subsection gives a genuine DOSE-RESPONSE across three trials: mean decreases in platelet count from baseline through Week 53 ranging from 6% (50 mg, Trials 2 and 3) to 10% (80 mg across all trials) in TRYNGOLZA-treated patients, whereas placebo-treated patients showed an increase of 22% in Trial 1 and no change in Trials 2 and 3; arm sizes TRYNGOLZA 50 mg N=354, 80 mg N=351, placebo N=356 (sHTG, Trials 2 NCT05079919 and 3 NCT05552326), and N=43 vs 23 in FCS Trial 1. Explicit negative safety statements usable as graded rows: the proportion of patients experiencing a bleeding adverse event was similar between TRYNGOLZA and placebo, and there were no major bleeding events associated with low platelet counts. Chemistry value: GalNAc-conjugated 2'-MOE gapmer showing a mild dose-dependent (grade-1) platelet decline — the clean middle of the bimodal rubric, between inotersen/volanesorsen (grade 3) and the grade-0 GalNAc-siRNAs. FDA review documents for this NDA are not yet posted beyond RiskR and OtherR (verified 404 on MedR/PharmR/MultidisciplineR), so the label is the sole regulatory locus for now.
title: FDA Prescribing Information — TRYNGOLZA (olezarsen) injection

data_description: Verified full text via efetch (96 KB XML, license CC BY). The long-term / post-monitoring-change arm of the inotersen record, and the evidence that enhanced monitoring converts a grade-3 risk into a managed grade-2 one - a genuinely useful contrast pair against the pre-monitoring NEURO-TTR rows. Extractable from the Results and Table 2 'Summary of treatment-emergent adverse events in the NEURO-TTR OLE': thrombocytopenia was the most common TEAE at 28.x% across all OLE patients; confirmed platelet count decreases below 100 x10^9/L in 25/50 (50%) of the placebo-inotersen group and 41/85 (48%) of the inotersen-inotersen group; dose interruption due to platelet monitoring rules in 32/85 (38%) inotersen-inotersen and 26/50 (52%) placebo-inotersen; grade 4 platelet count decrease reported in none of the patients in either group (cross-referenced to Online Resource 5, Fig.); two individual patients with nadir counts reported (one 43 x10^9/L at day 519, the other at day 350), neither permanently discontinuing; SAEs of thrombocytopenia n=4 in the inotersen-inotersen group. Table 2 also supplies the denominators (any TEAE 132/135 = 97.8%, TEAEs leading to permanent discontinuation 30 = 22.2%, to dose reduction 13 = 9.6%, to dose interruption/delay 66 = 48.9%).

data_description: Verified: SPL XML retrieved (210 KB) and the human-readable page returns HTTP 200. Olezarsen is the GalNAc-conjugated APOC3 successor to volanesorsen, so this label is the direct, same-target, same-sponsor evidence that conjugation converts a grade-3 dose-limiting signal into a grade-1 mild one - one of the most modelling-relevant contrasts available in this lane. Same subsection states the proportion of patients experiencing a bleeding adverse event was similar between TRYNGOLZA and placebo, and there were no major bleeding events associated with low platelet counts (clean grade-0/1 clinical-outcome rows). Section 6.1 Table (adverse reactions in FCS, incidence >5% and >3% higher than placebo) lists 'decreased platelet count' as one of the three most common adverse reactions, with per-arm n (%) counts alongside injection site reactions and arthralgia. Section 5 / Highlights repeat the decreased-platelet-count listing.

data_description: ABSTRACT VERIFIED AND READ IN FULL via efetch (liebertpub.com Cloudflare-403; Europe PMC 'Subscription required'; no PMC deposit; OpenAlex oa_status=closed). Shen, Wong, Oneda, Curtis, Schroeder, Zanardi, Engelhardt, Henry, Narayanan. The complement-crosstalk arm named in the lane brief, with the cleanest severe-thrombocytopenia animal model available. Extractable per-measurement values, locus 'Abstract': background incidence of severe TCP (platelets <50 K/uL) in Asian-sourced cynomolgus monkeys 2%-4% at doses >5 mg/kg/week; ISIS 405879 (2'-MOE ASO) at 40 mg/kg/week for 16 weeks induced severe TCP in 7 of 9 Mauritian-sourced monkeys and 0 of the Asian-sourced monkeys (a paired positive/negative row pair on one compound); marked increases in platelet-bound C3d/C4d in ALL thrombocytopenic Mauritian monkeys but NOT in unaffected Mauritian or Asian monkeys; the effect was independent of ASO-mediated fluid-phase alternative complement activation (an explicit negative mechanism row); correlation between serum anti-GPIIb/IIIa IgG and platelet reduction; increases in total serum IgM, anti-platelet IgM and anti-PF4 IgM in monkeys from both sources, more evident in Mauritian.
title: Complement C3d/C4d Deposition on Platelets Correlates with 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Antisense Oligonucleotide-Induced Thrombocytopenia in Monkeys

data_description: ABSTRACT VERIFIED AND READ IN FULL via efetch (liebertpub.com Cloudflare-403; Europe PMC 'Subscription required'; no PMC deposit). Henry, Narayanan, Shen, Bhanot, Younis, Burel. The source that establishes the two-phenotype framework the whole rubric rests on, and quantifies the animal-to-human translation gap for the rare severe form. Extractable per-measurement values, locus 'Abstract': NHP safety database spanning >102 independent 2'-MOE ASOs, 61 studies, >2,200 NHPs; phenotype 1 = consistent reproducible group-mean decrease in ~30% of compounds with counts typically remaining >=150 K/uL; phenotype 2 = sporadic decrease to <50 K/uL at 2%-4% incidence at doses >5 mg/kg, often not reproducible; ISIS 404173 chronic NHP study at 20 mg/kg/week for 26 weeks showed gradual group-mean decline at >=10 mg/kg/week plateauing by 13 weeks generally within normal range and maintained through 26 weeks; counts <50 K/uL in 1 of 16 NHP at 10 mg/kg/week and 3 of 16 NHP at 20 mg/kg/week; matched 26-week double-blind placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial, 62 patients on 200 mg/week ISIS 404173 (~3.3 mg/kg/week), increased incidence of >30% platelet decrease from baseline but ZERO incidence of platelet <75 K/uL — an explicit grade-0-for-severe human row against a positive NHP row on the same compound. Conclusion that NHPs over-predict the sporadic <50 K/uL event relative to humans.
title: Assessment of the Effects of 2'-Methoxyethyl Antisense Oligonucleotides on Platelet Count in Cynomolgus Nonhuman Primates

data_description: ABSTRACT VERIFIED AND READ IN FULL via efetch. Only the abstract is genuinely retrievable. This is the Narayanan mechanism paper named in the lane brief, and its abstract is unusually data-dense — ~9 distinct quantified readouts on a single compound, all locus 'Abstract': 12-week repeat-dose study, 5 cynomolgus monkeys, subcutaneous ISIS 104838 at 30-60 mg/kg/week, with 111In-oxine-labeled platelets for sequestration; platelet counts decreased 50%-90% by day 30 in ALL monkeys; total IgM increased 2- to 4.5-fold; anti-PF4 IgM increased 2- to 5-fold; anti-platelet IgM increased; monocyte chemotactic protein 1 increased; monocyte-derived extracellular vesicles increased 2- to 6-fold, indicating monocyte activation but explicitly NOT platelet activation (a negative activation row); von Willebrand factor antigen increased 2- to 3-fold in all monkeys with endothelial EV increases 2- to 4-fold in only 2 of 5; platelet sequestration in liver and spleen increased ~60-80%.
title: Investigation into the Mechanism(s) That Leads to Platelet Decreases in Cynomolgus Monkeys During Administration of ISIS 104838, a 2'-MOE-Modified Antisense Oligonucleotide

data_description: Verified: SPL XML retrieved (129 KB) and the human-readable page returns HTTP 200. Donidalorsen is a GalNAc-conjugated 2'-MOE PS ASO targeting prekallikrein (PKK/KLKB1) - the same target as ISIS 546254 / 721744 in the two Crooke pooled papers, so its rows join cleanly to them. Section 6.1, subsection 'Laboratory Tests - Decrease in Platelet Count' (following Table 1, adverse reactions with incidence >=5% and more common than placebo in OASIS-HAE), is fully quantitative and gives per-arm baseline and change values for three arms: mean platelet count at baseline 266,000/mm3 for DAWNZERA 80 mg every 4 weeks (N=45), 265,000/mm3 for 80 mg every 8 weeks (N=23), and 245,000/mm3 for placebo (N=22); mean percent change in platelet count at Week 25 of -9.6%, -7.9% and -1.4% respectively. Also states that across OASIS-HAE and 2 other clinical studies no DAWNZERA-treated patient had a platelet count below 50,000/mm3 and there were no major bleeding events associated with a low platelet count. This is a textbook grade-1 mild dose/schedule-dependent decline with an explicit dosing-frequency gradient (q4w vs q8w) and a matched placebo arm, all in one public-domain locus.

data_description: ABSTRACT VERIFIED AND READ IN FULL via efetch. RETRIEVABILITY CAVEAT: Europe PMC records the licence as 'cc by' but the article is NOT deposited in PMC, and both sciencedirect.com and jthjournal.org return 403 to curl and WebFetch — so despite the permissive licence only the abstract is actually retrievable in this session. The immune-clearance-pathway complement to the antibody-mediated sources: establishes an IVIg- and Syk-dependent platelet clearance mechanism, which is the effector arm the anti-platelet-antibody papers imply but do not demonstrate. Extractable content, locus 'Abstract', mostly comparative rather than numeric: BALB/c mice given titrated doses of ODN 2395 and ISIS 120704 both developed acute DOSE-DEPENDENT thrombocytopenia within 3 h and 24 h respectively, whereas saline and a 2'-O-methoxyethyl-modified antisense ODN control did NOT (a useful chemistry-contrast negative row); thrombocytopenia associated with significant plasma MCP-1 increases (echoing Narayanan 2018); IVIg, a Syk inhibitor, and TLR9 antagonists each significantly rescued the thrombocytopenia; in vitro CpG ODN activated human platelets, correlating significantly with enhanced IVIg- and Syk-dependent phagocytosis by THP-1 monocytes. Rows would carry readout_value TBD where the abstract reports direction and significance without a number.
title: CpG oligonucleotides induce acute murine thrombocytopenia dependent on toll-like receptor 9 and spleen tyrosine kinase pathways

data_description: CORRECTS A PREMISE IN THE LANE BRIEF. Full-text parse of the complete 67,141-character SPL returns ZERO occurrences of 'thrombocyt' and exactly ONE occurrence of 'platelet' — a Study exclusion criterion in sec 14 (patients with platelet count <=100,000/uL were not eligible for enrolment in ATLAS-OLE). Fitusiran therefore contributes a GRADE-0 platelet_count row, not a thrombocytopenia positive. Its hemostatic signal runs in the OPPOSITE direction and belongs in readout_category = coagulation: the Boxed Warning and sec 5.1 describe serious thrombotic events driven by antithrombin knockdown, with named risk factors (persistent AT activity <15%, the 80 mg once-monthly non-AT-based dose, indwelling venous catheters, post-operative setting when bleed-management guidelines are not followed); sec 2.2 gives the AT-driven dosing target (dose escalation considered if AT activity >35% at 6 months). Sec 6.1 exposure denominators: pooled N=335 fixed-dose + AT-DR, AT-DR N=286, median exposure 674 days (max 896); permanent discontinuations 4/286 (1.4%) including post-operative deep vein thrombosis and cerebral infarction. Useful as a mechanism-contrast control: a GalNAc-siRNA that perturbs hemostasis without touching platelet count.

data_description: VERIFIED: full-text XML 71,916 bytes. Human whole blood (PPACK- or CTI-anticoagulated) perfused over patterned collagen at 100/s in a microfluidic assay, treated with a panel of TLR ligands including a CpG oligodeoxynucleotide (TLR9 agonist). Fig 2 quantifies platelet deposition onto collagen per ligand; the text states clot buildup was 'strongly attenuated' by CpG ODN alongside imiquimod and poly(I:C); Fig 6 measures phosphatidylserine exposure under flow. This is a genuine human-whole-blood platelet-function readout for an oligonucleotide, and it is interesting because the direction is DECREASED platelet deposition, opposite to the GPVI-agonist behaviour reported elsewhere in this lane — useful as a contrasting row. RANKED LOW, honestly, for two reasons: only one oligonucleotide is involved so the row count is about 2-3, and critically the CpG ODN is identified only by supplier (Novus Biologicals) with NO sequence, length, backbone chemistry or class given, so an oligos.csv row would be almost entirely TBD and the compound cannot be reliably deduplicated against ODN2395/120704 elsewhere in the dataset. Include only if the extraction stage wants the contrasting direction; otherwise it is defensible to omit rather than pad. title: Activation of Most Toll-Like Receptors in Whole Human Blood Attenuates Platelet Deposition on Collagen under Flow (Liu et al.)

data_description: Small but genuinely unique: the ONLY regulatory document in this lane that reports a platelet finding for eplontersen. Sec 5.3 Preclinical safety data, verbatim: 'In a single monkey in the 13 week toxicity study, severely decreased platelet counts associated with spontaneous haemorrhage, presented as haematoma and petechiae, were observed at the highest dose tested (24 mg/kg/week).' The US Wainua label (SPL d7dcb847-71dd-4fff-82d0-d43a465fc096) contains no platelet content whatsoever, so this row exists only in the EU document. Scientifically load-bearing: eplontersen is the GalNAc-conjugated, lower-dose successor to inotersen against the same TTR target, and this pairs a grade-0 human clinical row with a grade-2/3 monkey row at a high multiple of the clinical dose — the same animal-over-predicts-human pattern the kidney dataset captures. Note the EU brand is Wainzua, not Wainua; the wainua EMA slug 404s. Whole document is 30 pp with exactly one platelet hit, so extraction is trivially verifiable.
title: EMA Wainzua (eplontersen) SmPC / Annex I Product Information
